title: Atomic Interaction Anchors — personal brainpad
content:
Overview

This is a personal sketchpad for a small product hypothesis: 'Atomic Interaction Anchors' (AIA). The core idea: instead of shipping entire conversation context or large prefix windows to the model, surface and store tiny, canonical "anchors" that encode the minimal interaction metadata and a compact semantic payload that can be reused across turns and different features (search, summarization, rerank). Anchors are intentionally small (tens to a few hundred tokens when expanded) and treated as first-class primitives in the session model.

Why this matters (problem statement)
- Cost: Many apps repeatedly re-send overlapping context across API calls. Even with prefix caching, we still pay for tokens or pay latency overhead reconstructing context.
- Latency: Building a long context window every request adds CPU and memory pressure on clients and on the runtime.
- UX: Features like conversation shortcuts, reusable snippets, and cross-session recall feel brittle because they rely on opaque blobs or full transcripts.
- Quality: When context includes redundant or noisy turns, model focus degrades. Anchors aim to surface the semantically salient bits only.

Design goals
1) Minimal: anchors should be cheap to store and retrieve (both network and token cost).
2) Composable: anchors can be stitched together in arbitrary order to build a lightweight context for a given request.
3) Deterministic semantics: each anchor has a small structured header that describes type, relevance score, timestamp, and a stable id.
4) Portable: anchors work across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; encoding format should be versioned and small.
5) Observable: we can trace which anchors influenced outputs and measure quality impact.

Core concept (rough spec)
- Anchor = {id, kind, short-text, embedding-id, compact-metadata}
  - id: stable short string (anchor_....)
  - kind: e.g., "intent-snippet", "fact", "user-profile", "task-history", "short-cut"
  - short-text: 1–3 sentence human readable canonicalization
  - embedding-id: pointer to lightweight vector store entry (deduped)
  - compact-metadata: small tag list, relevance weight, created_at

Behavioral rules and APIs (brain-draft)
1) CreateAnchor API (session-scoped or global): client provides raw selection or model-suggested snippet + optional canonicalizer transform. Server returns anchor id and small tokenized payload.
2) FetchAnchors(ids[], policy): returns anchor payloads plus age/relevance. Policy can ask for expanded tokenized form vs compressed summary.
3) ComposeContext(anchors[], budget_tokens): server selects top-k anchors, expands just enough of each anchor to fit budget, returns ordered prompts + orchestration hints (e.g., "put user profile first, then facts").
4) TraceInfluence(request_id) -> anchor_ids with contribution weight (for observability).

User stories (early)
- As a mobile chat product engineer, I want to save a short user "preference anchor" so I don't re-send the full profile on every message.
- As an app designer, I want authors to tag a turn as a "decision" anchor so downstream reranker and summarizer can prioritize it.
- As an SRE, I want a way to evict rarely used anchors from hot cache while keeping stable ids for retrieval.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Creation + retrieval APIs implemented in hosted runtime with <10ms local lookup for hot anchors.
- ComposeContext returns <= configured token budget and selects anchors deterministically based on relevance score.
- End-to-end comparison: using anchors reduces average tokens per request by >=15% on two sample features (FAQ followups, personalized greetings) without hurting top-1 accuracy measured on a micro-eval.
- Basic observability: trace shows per-anchor contribution and usage heatmap in Console for a sample customer.

Telemetry & metrics to track
- anchor_create_rate, anchor_fetch_latency, anchor_hit_rate (hot vs cold), avg_tokens_saved_per_request, quality_regression_delta (micro-eval), anchors_per_session_distribution, stagnation_age_distribution (how old anchors are when used).

UX sketches & flows (notes)
- Console: a lightweight anchor inspector -> search anchors by id, text, or tag; preview expanded tokenized snippet.
- SDK: client stores local anchor handles (id + cached short-text) and sends only ids when allowed; fallback to full text when anchor not found server-side.
- Prompt assembly policy: before model call, call ComposeContext(anchors, budget) and append a compact "anchor map" as a structured hint so model can request clarifications if needed.

Open questions / risks
- Canonicalization: Who owns the canonical short-text? Model or client? (Prefer allow both: client-provided canonicalization for deterministic UIs, model-normalized optional secondary field.)
- Security/PII: anchors could encode sensitive facts. Need KMS/HSM hooks and clear TTL/eviction policies, plus redaction tooling.
- Cost tradeoff: anchors add an index/service layer; need to ensure net savings after storage/lookup costs.
- Versioning: format must be backward compatible; add format_version in header and migration plan.
- Evaluation: how to measure "influence" robustly across diverse prompts? Consider embedding similarity + logit attribution later.

Implementation sketch (tech notes)
- Storage: small-tier vector store for embeddings + metadata store (key-value). Hot cache in-memory (Redis) with LRU; cold fetch from blob store for expanded payload.
- Encoding: short-text stored verbatim; expanded tokens stored as compressed delta (token ids) to save space.
- Retrieval: ComposeContext runs a lightweight ranker combining embedding-similarity and metadata weights; then greedy pack anchors until token budget reached.
- Model-side hints: include an "anchor index block" at the start of prompt that enumerates anchors with ids and condensed descriptions so the model can reference by id in its answer.

Next steps (practical)
- Quick prototype: implement CreateAnchor + FetchAnchors + ComposeContext in a dev runtime (2 engineer-weeks).
- Micro-evals: design 3 short evals (personalized greeting, followup clarification, instruction re-use) and measure token usage + quality.
- UX: wire basic Inspector in Console and add a developer flag to opt-in per-API-key.
- Security: draft policy for TTL defaults and redaction flow; flag for "sensitive" anchor kind requiring encryption.

To-do (me)
- Paper sketch for header fields and wire-level schema (today)
- Wire a prototyping GH branch and PR template (next week)
- Reach out to Maya for micro-eval designs and to Noah for SRE cost/backpressure thresholds

Random notes and heuristics (scratch)
- Anchor kinds maybe map to storage tiers: "ephemeral" (short TTL), "session" (short-term), "persistent" (user-managed).
- Consider delta-anchors: store differences from a profile anchor to further compress updates.
- Maybe integrate with Redwood "compact-snapshot" experiment (if exists) so anchor lifecycle can reuse existing snapshot machinery.

End of pad. This is intentionally rough — thinking out loud. Will polish into a short PRD after initial prototype results.
